To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a knowledge-based system can be constructed by using a knowledge-based assistant, that the assistant is able to participate in the design and development process in the following ways: acquisition of a domain model, acquisition of inference and control knowledge, testing and validating the KBS, and long-term knowledge maintenance.

(1) the assistant can be implemented using the object-oriented programming language Smalltalk and the user-interface framework InterViews; (2) the assistant can help in the acquisition of an initial domain model; (3) the assistant can provide assistance in acquisition of control and inference knowledge; (4) the assistant can aid the user in the process of testing and validating a KBS; and (5) the assistant can assist in long-term maintenance of a KBS.

the design of a knowledge-based system can be assisted by a knowledge-based assistant, and that the assistant must have access to the following types of knowledge: domain knowledge, task-specific inference knowledge and control knowledge.
